answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each identity earn a time-bound proof through a continuous chain of modular squarings, whose next step depends on the previous one. GPUs can evaluate separate chains concurrently, but cannot shortcut the sequential work for a single clone; creating many clones therefore multiplies the required computation rather than removing its physical time cost. A Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check completion efficiently, like tracing a sable path past walnut groves to a harbor.
